newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mainly softer.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mainly softer.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were unchanged to easier on Monday, traders said.
Outright gas oil prices slid $6.75 a tonne on easier futures, dragged lower by warmer weather in northern Europe.
A cargo of 0.2 percent heating oil with -5 cloud property and -15 cold filter plugging point traded at cif high Med quotes +$1.25, basis Koper, for Feburary 5-9 delivery, traders said.

But Russian heating oil remained long, with a healthy supply and few buyers. Shipping remains very tight, keeping rates for voyages across the Med at over Worldscale 300. Russian is on offer at cif high quotes Med +$1.50/2 basis Genoa.
That was $1 easier than last week, but no buyers were seen.
Gasoline prices were unchanged but underpinned by healthy arbitrage demand to the U.S., which sucked up one to 1.5 million tonnes of regular unleaded in the first half of January from the Med.
"There is quite good demand for low octane from all Med destinations," an Italian trader added.
Naphtha was slightly lower as high freight rates continued to hamper deals and limit arbitrage, and shift the focus to February demand.
"There are no vessels," said one trader.
High sulphur fuel oil was a couple of dollars softer as prices in NWE slumped again but the market was very thin and relatively balanced.
Low sulphur fuel oil was softer again, amid few fresh signs of Italian demand.

France's General Labour Confederation, the biggest union at state utility EdF and Gaz de France, called a 24-hour strike for Wednesday. Traders said this would have little impact on fuel oil prices, although some said they had detected increased local demand for fuel oil from EdF.
